skill.name: never-twice
skill.description: Guide AI assistants to maintain a shared error log, verify facts, plan reversible work, and provide evidence before reporting completion.
skill.summary: Reduce repeated mistakes with topic-based error reviews, source verification, and evidence-backed completion checks.
skill.author: rabbitdesigns22

content.user_title: Reduce Repeated AI Mistakes with an Error Log
content.value_statement: Repeated mistakes and unsupported completion claims waste time across AI sessions. This skill guides assistants to review previous errors, verify facts, and document evidence.
actual_capabilities: Defines a shared error-log format containing the date, topic, mistake, root cause, and prevention rule.
Directs assistants to review relevant error entries and existing project decisions before starting work.
Requires source checks for factual claims and explicit disclosure when important facts cannot be verified.
Prompts planning around failure modes, reversibility, action order, and required user input.
Requires completion evidence, such as passing tests or records read back after saving.
Directs assistants to record new mistakes and add project-specific rules to project notes.
limitations: Provides written instructions, not an executable validator or automatic error-tracking service.
Cross-session continuity depends on access to the same saved error log.
Verification depends on available tools, source access, and assistant compliance.
Cannot guarantee perfect answers or prevent every repeated mistake.

use_cases.title: Review Previous Development Mistakes
use_cases.description: Check relevant error entries before changing code, then use tests and concrete evidence to support completion claims.

use_cases.title: Verify Operational Status Reports
use_cases.description: Confirm identifiers, metrics, and status meanings against source records before reporting conclusions.

use_cases.title: Preserve Project Lessons Between Sessions
use_cases.description: Record recurring client-project mistakes with root causes and prevention rules for later task reviews.

prompt_templates.title: Review Relevant Lessons
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the shared error log for [topic]. Summarize relevant mistakes and prevention rules before starting this task.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Reported Fact
prompt_templates.prompt: Check [claim] against [source]. Report the evidence and mark anything that cannot be verified.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: validate a fact or status.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Evidence-Based Completion
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan [task] using relevant error-log entries. Identify failure modes, reversible steps, needed user input, and the evidence required before reporting completion.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare a task with operational consequences.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve and Document a Recurring Error
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate [recurring error] using the log and source evidence. Fix it, verify the result, and record its root cause and prevention rule.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: complete a correction and preserve the lesson.

output_examples.input: Review the sales metric label before recommending a change.
output: Previous lesson: a sales label included booked calls without saying so.
Verification needed: inspect the calculation and the code that renders the label.
Recommendation remains unverified until those sources establish what the metric counts.

output_examples.input: What evidence is needed before calling a status-label fix complete?
output: Confirm the label against the source field and its documented meaning.
Run relevant tests and inspect the updated interface.
Record the root cause and a prevention rule in the shared error log.
Report any verification that could not be completed.

best_practices: Keep entries concise and searchable by topic, with a clear root cause and prevention rule.
Use current source evidence instead of treating an old log entry as proof of present behavior.
Keep the shared log accessible to authorized sessions and exclude secrets or unnecessary client details.
anti_patterns: Assuming the skill guarantees perfect answers or eliminates the need for independent review.
Reporting completion without checking the relevant result.
Recording vague complaints without an actionable prevention rule.

faq.question: Does this skill guarantee that mistakes never repeat?
faq.answer: No. It provides a structured review process, but outcomes depend on evidence, available tools, and consistent use.

faq.question: Where does the error log live?
faq.answer: The skill suggests a shared file such as ERRORS.md at the workspace root.

faq.question: What belongs in each error entry?
faq.answer: Include the date, topic, what happened, root cause, and a rule intended to prevent recurrence.

faq.question: Does it include scripts or a hosted service?
faq.answer: No. The provided skill consists of Markdown instructions for an assistant to follow.

faq.question: What happens when a fact cannot be verified?
faq.answer: The assistant should mark it as not verified and explain how it could be checked.

faq.question: Does the log persist across sessions automatically?
faq.answer: The file must be saved and remain accessible. The skill does not provide synchronization or separate storage.
